paper.title: 3GPP TS 35.202, Specification of the 3GPP Confidentiality and Integrity Algorithms; Document 2: KASUMI Specification (Release 16), with TS 35.203 Implementors' Test Data
authors: 3GPP / ETSI SAGE (algorithm designed on the basis of MISTY1)
paper.venue: ETSI TS 135 202 and TS 135 203 V16.0.0, August 2020

program.how: written for ounce-core from the algorithm in the paper or specification; no third-party code copied
program.target: static freestanding aarch64 Linux ELF, run with `ounce-core run-elf`

claims_checked: KASUMI (8-round Feistel with FL, FO and FI, S7/S9 tables, key schedule with the C1-C8 constants) written from TS 35.202 reproduces TS 35.203 test sets 1-3: for each, all 64 round subkeys, every FL input/output (8), FO input/output (8), FI input/key/output (24 calls) and every FI 7-bit and 9-bit data-path value (24 calls x 12), plus the 64-bit output: 474 published values per set, 1,422 in all
Test set 4 (50 chained encryptions meant to touch every S-box entry) gives the published 738BAD4C4A690802
The specification's two worked S-box examples S7[38] = 58 and S9[138] = 339

expected_values_source.what: 3GPP TS 35.202 (S-box tables, key constants, structure) and TS 35.203 (test sets with intermediate values)
expected_values_source.note: tables and test values were extracted from the PDF text by script and compiled in as data; the program was written from the specification text. Only the KASUMI block cipher is checked, not the f8/f9 modes in TS 35.203 sections 4 and 5, and not the S-box gate-logic equations

negative_control: built with -DKAS_CFLIP=1 (the low bit of every key-schedule constant flipped), 1,262 of 1,426 compared values mismatch, test set 4 fails and the program exits 1
not_checked: the f8 (confidentiality) and f9 (integrity) algorithms and their test data, which use KASUMI as a building block
the S-box tables against the gate-logic formulas given beside them (only the two worked examples)
security claims of KASUMI (including published attacks on it) and speed
Tier-4 and native ARM64 execution (the native comparison is x86-64)
what_a_pass_means: this program, run on ounce-core, produces exactly the 1,425 values the 3GPP KASUMI specification and its test data publish. It does not show the security claims hold.
